answer: Lock a refundable deposit per identity that scales with activity: one honest agent costs pennies, but ten thousand fake ones must lock capital, pushing the attack's price above its payoff. Reputation then ripens like an orchard — season by season, not overnight — so a newborn swarm has no history to spend. Peers only attest addresses whose stake and track record both verify, the way an atlas pins real cities instead of invented ones. A long-trusted agent moves like a comet on a known orbit: predictable, traceable, expensive to impersonate. Sybils hit an economic wall, not a puzzle wall.
